intended_object: The tensor product bifunctor ⊗ : FGComod_C × FGComod_C → FGComod_C on finitely generated right comodules over a bialgebra C over a commutative semiring R. It sends (M, N) to M ⊗_R N with the diagonal coaction m⊗n ↦ (m₀⊗n₀)⊗m₁n₁, and (f, g) to f ⊗ g. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is a functor from the product category. On objects it gives `tensor R C P.1 P.2`, which is the full-subcategory object on `M ⊗[R] N`. Its coaction comes from `Comodule.tensor`, which is `tensorCombine ∘ (coact ⊗ coact)`. That is the standard diagonal coaction, built from the multiplication of the bialgebra. On morphisms it gives `tensorMap`, which is `TensorProduct.map f g` packaged as a comodule morphism. The functor laws are proved from `tensorMap_id` and `tensorMap_comp`. So this is the usual tensor bifunctor on finitely generated comodules.

The generality is right. The diagonal coaction needs a bialgebra structure, and R is only required to be a commutative semiring, which is as general as the construction allows. Finiteness is preserved because a tensor product of finitely generated modules is finitely generated (Mathlib's `Module.Finite.tensorProduct`).

Mathlib at this commit has no comodules and no comodule categories, so there is no counterpart to cite.
